title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco FMC Flaws to Gain Root Access and Deploy Malware
content_md: Cisco Talos warns that threat actors are actively exploiting two vulnerabilities in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software, including a critical authentication-bypass flaw that can give unauthenticated remote attackers root-level access to affected appliances. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-20079, carries a CVSS score of 10.0. It lets attackers bypass authentication on unpatched Cisco Secure FMC instances and run scripts that ultimately grant root access to the underlying operating system. A second flaw, CVE-2026-20316, has a CVSS score of 5.3 and permits remote login through a low-privileged static account. Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco FMC Flaws While the latter vulnerability is rated moderate, Talos said attackers are chaining it with other FMC flaws to escalate privileges, execute malicious packages, and expand access into victim networks. Talos identified three separate clusters of post-compromise activity involving state-linked and financially motivated attackers . The first cluster, tracked as UAT-12197, exploited CVE-2026-20079 to deploy a JSP-based web shell in the CSM Tomcat webroot directory. The web shell Base64-decodes a parameter named “F6C1F0E7” and loads a Java class in the FMC Java process. Attackers subsequently placed a malicious cmd.jar file on the system.
